examples.ko: 이 휴대폰 판매점은 일요일에도 문을 열어요.
examples.en: This phone shop is open on Sundays too.
A new shop opened near my house.
I tried it out at the shop and bought it.

examples.ko: 인터넷보다 판매점에 가는 게 더 편해요.
examples.en: Going to a shop is more convenient than the internet.
Thank you for visiting our store.

examples.ko: 친구가 일하는 판매점도 이번 주에 세일을 해요.
examples.en: The shop where my friend works is also having a sale this week.

explain: 판매점은 '휴대폰 판매점', '자동차 판매점'처럼 앞에 파는 물건을 붙여서 써요. 여러 물건을 파는 보통 가게는 그냥 '가게'라고 해요.
explain_en: 판매점 usually comes after the product, as in '휴대폰 판매점' (phone shop) or '자동차 판매점' (car dealer). An ordinary shop that sells many things is simply called '가게'.

examples.ko: 너무 힘들어서 회사를 관둘까 생각 중이에요.
examples.en: It is so hard that I am thinking about quitting my job.
My younger sibling quit the academy they were attending.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 아르바이트를 관두고 여행을 갈 거예요.
examples.en: Next month I will quit my part-time job and go traveling.
If you don't want to do it, it's fine to quit now.
I told the manager the reason I am quitting.
I never give up halfway.

explain: '그만두다'를 줄여서 말할 때 쓰는 형태예요. 편하게 말할 때 쓰고, 윗사람에게 하는 말이나 글에서는 '그만두다'가 더 알맞아요. '관둬요', '관뒀어요'처럼 '둬'로 바뀌는 활용에 주의하세요.
explain_en: It is the shortened form of '그만두다' used in casual speech. With superiors or in writing, '그만두다' fits better. Watch the conjugation, which changes to '둬': '관둬요', '관뒀어요'.

examples.en: I'm worried because I have no income these days.
My father works from dawn to make a living.

examples.ko: 이 일은 돈벌이는 괜찮지만 너무 힘들어요.
examples.en: The pay in this job is decent, but it is too hard.
He is only interested in making money.
Making money matters, but health matters more.
Work I started to earn money became a hobby.

explain: '돈벌이가 좋다', '돈벌이가 안 되다'처럼 일로 버는 수입이 얼마나 되는지 말할 때 써요. '벌이'라고 짧게도 하고, '수입'은 더 공식적인 표현이에요.
explain_en: Use it to talk about how much a job earns: '돈벌이가 좋다' (pays well), '돈벌이가 안 되다' (doesn't pay). It can be shortened to '벌이', and '수입' is the more formal word.

examples.en: After washing my hair, I always use conditioner.
The conditioner has run out, so I have to buy some.
I only apply conditioner to the ends of my hair.
Shall I buy conditioner too?
I make my hair soft with conditioner.

examples.ko: 샤워할 때 린스 대신 트리트먼트를 써요.
examples.en: In the shower I use a treatment instead of conditioner.

explain: 샴푸로 머리를 감은 다음에 바르는 제품이에요. 한국에서 '린스'와 '컨디셔너'는 보통 같은 제품으로 봐요. '린스를 바르다', '린스를 헹구다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the product you apply after washing hair with shampoo. In Korea '린스' and '컨디셔너' are usually treated as the same product. Say '린스를 바르다' to apply it.

examples.en: The stars twinkle in the night sky.
After I cleaned, the floor shone.
The glittering marbles are so pretty.
The child's eyes are sparkling.

examples.ko: 새로 산 구두가 반짝반짝해서 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: My new shoes are shiny, so I feel good.
I wiped the window until it sparkled.

explain: 별이나 보석이 빛나는 모습에도 쓰고, 깨끗이 닦은 바닥이나 유리가 빛나는 모습에도 써요. '별이 반짝반짝 빛나요'처럼 '하다' 없이 부사로도 써요.
explain_en: Use it for stars and jewels that twinkle, and also for a floor or glass that shines after cleaning. You can also use '반짝반짝' alone as an adverb: '별이 반짝반짝 빛나요'.

examples.ko: 사진가는 하루 종일 산에서 해를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The photographer waited for the sun on the mountain all day.
A famous photographer came to our school.
I am a student who dreams of becoming a photographer.
I asked a photographer to take our family photo.

examples.ko: 그 사진가의 전시회가 다음 주에 열려요.
examples.en: That photographer's exhibition opens next week.
My father's friend works as a travel photographer.

explain: 사진을 찍는 일을 직업으로 하는 사람을 말할 때 써요. 같은 일을 하는 사람을 '사진작가'라고도 하고, 사진관에서 일하는 사람은 '사진사'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who takes photos as a profession. The same person may also be called '사진작가', and someone working at a photo studio is sometimes called '사진사'.

examples.en: Hey, what do you think you're doing?
The boss called out, 'Hey, Assistant Manager Kim!'
In the drama, he shouted, 'Hey! Stop right there!'

examples.ko: 아저씨가 '이봐 학생' 하고 저를 불러 세웠어요.
examples.en: A man called out 'Hey, student' and stopped me.

examples.ko: '이봐, 이봐!' 하고 누가 저를 계속 불러요.
examples.en: Someone keeps calling me, 'Hey, hey!'

examples.ko: 옛날 영화에서는 '이봐, 친구' 하고 말을 거는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: In old movies there are scenes where someone says, 'Hey, pal.'

explain: 친구나 아랫사람을 부를 때 쓰는 말투라서, 윗사람이나 처음 보는 어른에게 쓰면 무례하게 들릴 수 있어요. 낯선 사람을 정중하게 부를 때는 '저기요'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used to call a friend or someone younger or lower in rank, so with an elder or a stranger it can sound rude. To politely get a stranger's attention, use '저기요'.

examples.en: Grandmother sings while playing the janggu.
There is a janggu in the room.

examples.ko: 장구는 양쪽 면을 쳐서 소리를 내요.
examples.en: A janggu makes sound when you hit its two sides.

examples.ko: 학교 동아리에서 장구도 배우고 노래도 불러요.
examples.en: In the school club I learn the janggu and sing too.
Make a lively rhythm with the janggu.
In samulnori, people dance to the janggu.

explain: 한국 전통 악기로, 가운데가 잘록한 모양의 북이에요. 양쪽 면을 쳐서 소리를 내요. 사물놀이에서 쓰는 악기 중 하나예요.
explain_en: It is a traditional Korean drum with a narrow waist in the middle. You hit both sides to make sound. It is one of the instruments used in samulnori.

examples.en: You can see kangaroos in Australia.
At the zoo I saw a kangaroo hopping.
We lined up to see the baby kangaroo.
I want to jump high like a kangaroo.
I gave a kangaroo doll to my younger sibling as a present.
I put up pictures of a kangaroo and a koala on the wall.

explain: 동물 이름이지만 '캥거루족'이라는 말로도 들려요. 어른이 되어서도 부모와 함께 살며 도움을 받는 사람을 가리켜요.

phrases.example: 서른이 넘어도 부모님 집에 사는 캥거루족이 늘고 있어요.
phrases.en: adult who keeps living off their parents
phrases.nuance_ko: 어른이 되어서도 부모에게 기대어 사는 사람을 가리켜요. 놀리는 느낌이 있어서 다른 사람에게 쓸 때는 조심해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to adults who keep living with and relying on their parents. It has a teasing tone, so be careful using it about others.

explain_en: It is an animal name, but you also hear it in '캥거루족', which refers to adults who keep living with and relying on their parents.

en: go on a field trip; visit; tour

examples.en: The students are touring a factory.
Last week we visited a museum on a field trip.
Next month we will tour a broadcasting station.
I toured the company and talked with a staff member.
The children touring the farm look happy.

examples.ko: 신문사를 견학해서 기사가 어떻게 만들어지는지 알았어요.
examples.en: I toured a newspaper company and learned how articles are made.

explain: 공부나 일에 도움이 되도록 공장, 박물관, 회사 같은 곳에 가서 직접 보고 배울 때 써요. 그냥 구경하러 갈 때는 '구경하다'를 써요. '견학을 가다'처럼도 말해요.
explain_en: Use it when you visit a factory, museum or company to see and learn firsthand. For just sightseeing, use '구경하다'. You can also say '견학을 가다'.

examples.en: Graduate students study in the lab until late at night.
My older brother is a graduate student, so he is very busy.
A new dormitory for graduate students has opened.
I asked a graduate student for Korean lessons.
I met my graduate student friend at the library.
I will become a graduate student next year.

explain: 대학교를 졸업한 뒤 더 깊이 공부하는 사람이에요. '대학생'과 달리 석사나 박사 과정을 공부해요. '대학원 다녀요'라고 말하는 경우도 있어요.
explain_en: This is someone who keeps studying after finishing university. Unlike a '대학생', they study in a master's or doctoral program. People also say '대학원 다녀요' (I attend grad school).

examples.en: Yesterday's soccer match ended in a tie.
The two teams ended up in a tie.
It's a pity that this match was a tie.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 이번 시즌에 무승부를 두 번 기록했어요.
examples.en: Our team drew twice this season.
Because the game was a tie, everyone applauded.
In a tie, each team gets one point.

explain: 경기가 같은 점수로 끝났을 때 쓰는 명사라서 '무승부가 되다', '무승부로 끝나다'처럼 써요. 같은 상황의 동사는 '비기다'예요. '승리', '패배'와 나란히 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It is a noun for a game that ends with equal scores, used as '무승부가 되다' or '무승부로 끝나다'. The verb for the same situation is '비기다'. Learn it together with '승리' (win) and '패배' (loss).

examples.en: He was called a traitor by his friends.
The traitor in the movie was revealed at the end.

examples.ko: 저는 배신자라는 말을 듣고 많이 속상했어요.
examples.en: I was very upset to be called a traitor.

examples.ko: 그는 회사의 비밀을 알려 준 배신자예요.
examples.en: He is the traitor who gave away the company's secrets.
It is not easy to forgive a betrayer.

examples.ko: 아무도 배신자와 같이 일하고 싶어 하지 않아요.
examples.en: Nobody wants to work with a traitor.

explain: 믿던 사람을 속이거나 등진 사람을 가리킬 때 써요. 친구나 동료에게 쓰면 아주 강한 비난이라서 조심해야 해요. '변절자'는 주로 생각이나 편을 바꾼 사람에게 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a person who deceived or turned against someone who trusted them. Calling a friend or colleague this is a very strong accusation, so be careful. '변절자' is mainly for someone who switched beliefs or sides.

examples.en: We learned about the Roman Empire in world history class.

examples.ko: 저는 세계사에 관심이 많아서 책을 많이 읽어요.
examples.en: I am very interested in world history, so I read many books.
World history is hard because there is a lot to memorize.
I study Korean history and world history together.

examples.ko: 이 시험은 세계사에서 문제가 많이 나와요.
examples.en: This test has many questions from world history.
I want to learn world history too.

explain: 학교에서는 '한국사'와 따로 배우는 과목 이름이기도 해요. 그래서 '한국사와 세계사'처럼 둘을 같이 말하는 때가 많아요.
explain_en: At school it is also the name of a subject taught separately from '한국사' (Korean history). That is why the two often appear together: '한국사와 세계사'.

examples.en: I study English literature at university.
We read Shakespeare in English literature class.
My older sister graduated from the English literature department and became a translator.
I borrowed a book about English literature from the library.
English literature is fun too, but I like Korean literature more.

examples.ko: 영문학이 어렵다는 친구도 있고 쉽다는 친구도 있어요.
examples.en: Some friends say English literature is hard and others say it is easy.

explain: 대학교 전공 이름으로 써요. 나라 이름을 줄여 '문학'을 붙이는 방식은 '국문학'(한국 문학), '불문학'(프랑스 문학)에도 보여요. 전공 학과는 '영문학과'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used as a university major. Abbreviating the country name and adding '문학' also appears in '국문학' (Korean literature) and '불문학' (French literature). The department is '영문학과'.

examples.en: A cowboy rides a horse and herds cattle.
Cowboys appear in Western movies.

examples.ko: 아이가 카우보이 모자를 쓰고 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: The child wore a cowboy hat and took a photo.
I watched a movie with a cowboy as the hero.
My uncle wears boots like a cowboy.
Even a cowboy gets tired after working all day.

explain: 영어 cowboy에서 온 외래어로, 미국 서부에서 말을 타고 소를 키우는 사람을 떠올리게 해요. '카우보이 모자', '카우보이 부츠'처럼 뒤에 다른 말을 붙여 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: A loanword from English 'cowboy', it calls to mind people on horseback raising cattle in the American West. It is often followed by another word: '카우보이 모자' (cowboy hat), '카우보이 부츠' (cowboy boots).

examples.en: I wore jeans for the bottoms.
I matched the colors of the top and bottom.
This store sells bottoms separately.
The bottoms are too long, so I need to have them shortened.
I wear comfortable bottoms when I exercise.
A stain got on the bottoms, so I took them to the laundry.

explain: '상의'(윗옷)의 짝말이에요. 바지와 치마를 함께 가리키는 말이라 옷 가게나 쇼핑몰에서 볼 수 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '바지', '치마'처럼 구체적인 이름을 써도 돼요.
explain_en: It is the partner of '상의' (top). It covers pants and skirts together, so you see it in clothing shops and online stores. In everyday talk you can use specific words like '바지' or '치마'.

examples.en: I fell and my ribs hurt.
The doctor checked my ribs.

examples.ko: 갈비뼈는 가슴 속 장기를 지켜 줘요.
examples.en: The ribs protect the organs inside the chest.
My rib area hurt, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 갈비뼈에 금이 가서 한 달 동안 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I cracked a rib and rested for a month.
I had an X-ray taken to see whether the ribs were hurt too.

explain: '갈비'는 먹는 고기 이름으로 더 잘 알려져 있어요. 몸 안의 뼈를 말할 때는 '갈비뼈'라고 하고, 다쳤을 때는 '갈비뼈에 금이 가다', '갈비뼈가 부러지다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: '갈비' is better known as a cut of meat to eat. For the bone in the body, say '갈비뼈'. When injured: '갈비뼈에 금이 가다' (crack a rib), '갈비뼈가 부러지다' (break a rib).

examples.en: As the sun set, the sky turned golden.
I saw a child with golden hair.
The autumn fields are golden.

examples.ko: 저녁 햇살의 금빛은 사진에 잘 담기지 않아요.
examples.en: The golden color of evening sunlight doesn't come out well in photos.
Golden leaves blow in the wind.
I received a ring with a golden tint as a gift.

explain: 금처럼 빛나는 노란색을 말할 때 써요. '금색'과 비슷하지만 '-빛'이 붙어서 빛나는 느낌이 더 있어요. 노을, 머리카락, 곡식 밭처럼 풍경을 그릴 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Use it for a shiny, gold-like yellow. It is close to '금색', but the '-빛' ending adds a feeling of shining light. It suits scenery such as sunsets, hair, and grain fields.

examples.en: In spring I sneeze because of pollen.
Pollen blew in the wind and piled up on the car.
Pollen can cause allergies.
Bees collect pollen and carry it home.
People sensitive to pollen wear masks.
The weather news reports the pollen level too.

explain: 봄에 '꽃가루 알레르기'나 '꽃가루 농도'처럼 건강과 날씨 이야기에서 같이 들어요. 한자어로는 '화분'이라고도 하는데, '화분'은 꽃을 심은 그릇도 가리켜서 헷갈릴 수 있어요.
explain_en: You hear it with health and weather topics in spring, like '꽃가루 알레르기' (pollen allergy) or '꽃가루 농도' (pollen count). The Sino-Korean word is '화분', but that also means a flowerpot, so it can be confusing.

examples.en: I can hear a siren far away.
An ambulance passed by with its siren going.
When the siren sounded, the cars made way.
A siren in the middle of the night startled me awake.
The police car arrived quietly without a siren.
A siren quickly grabs people's attention.

explain: 구급차, 소방차, 경찰차에서 나는 소리와 그 장치를 모두 가리켜요. 소리가 날 때는 '사이렌이 울리다', 소리를 내게 할 때는 '사이렌을 울리다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It means both the sound made by ambulances, fire trucks and police cars and the device itself. When it sounds, say '사이렌이 울리다'; when someone sets it off, '사이렌을 울리다'.

examples.en: I paint watercolors every weekend.
For watercolors, you mix in a lot of water.
The watercolor hanging on the wall is really pretty.
I painted a seascape in watercolor.
Watercolor paint spreads easily.
I want to learn both watercolor and oil painting.

explain: 물에 푼 물감으로 그리는 그림을 가리켜요. 기름 물감으로 그리는 그림은 '유화'라고 해요. 그린다고 말할 때는 '수채화를 그리다'를 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a painting made with paint thinned in water. A painting made with oil paint is '유화'. To say you paint one, use '수채화를 그리다'.

examples.ko: 이 도서관은 책을 빌리면 스탬프를 찍어 줘요.
examples.en: This library stamps your book when you borrow it.

examples.ko: 스탬프가 번져서 글자가 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The stamp smudged, so the letters are hard to see.
Collecting stamps in my passport is my hobby.

examples.ko: 카페에서 커피를 사면 스탬프 한 개를 줘요.
examples.en: If you buy coffee at the cafe, they give you one stamp.
The children made a pretty picture with stamps.
After using a stamp, I close the lid.

explain: '도장'과 비슷하지만, 이름을 확인하는 용도는 보통 '도장'이라고 해요. 그림이나 모양이 있는 기념용·장식용은 '스탬프'라고 해요. 카페의 '스탬프 쿠폰'도 이 말이에요.
explain_en: It is similar to '도장', but a stamp used to confirm a name is usually called '도장'. A commemorative or decorative stamp with a picture or shape is a '스탬프'. A cafe's '스탬프 쿠폰' uses this word too.

examples.ko: 작업장은 아침 여덟 시에 문을 열어요.
examples.en: The workshop opens at eight in the morning.
The factory work area is too hot.
You must wear a helmet inside the work area.
My father makes furniture in his workshop.
I tidied up the workshop and went home.
It is the day we move to the new workshop.

explain: 공장이나 공방처럼 손이나 기계로 물건을 만드는 곳을 가리켜요. '일터'는 일하는 곳 전체를 넓게 부르고, '작업장'은 작업이 이루어지는 구체적인 공간을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: It refers to a place like a factory or workshop where things are made by hand or machine. '일터' is a broad word for any place of work, while '작업장' points to the specific space where the work happens.

examples.en: I went to a seaside guesthouse with my family.
The guesthouse is clean and quiet.
I booked a guesthouse with my friends.

examples.ko: 이 펜션은 마당에서 바비큐를 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: At this guesthouse you can have a barbecue in the yard.
I stayed one night at a guesthouse and came back.
You have to book a guesthouse just like a hotel.

explain: 한국에서 '펜션'은 보통 산이나 바다 근처에 있는 작은 숙소예요. 영어 'pension'은 보통 연금을 가리키니까 한국어 쓰임과 달라요. 한 채를 빌려 가족이나 친구끼리 묵는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: In Korea '펜션' is usually a small lodging near mountains or the sea. The English word 'pension' normally means a retirement pension, so the Korean usage is different. Families or friends often rent a whole house.

examples.ko: 핸드볼은 손으로 공을 던져 골을 넣어요.
examples.en: In handball, you throw the ball by hand to score goals.
I played handball for the first time at school.
I watched a handball match on TV.
My younger sibling says they want to be a handball player.
Handball has goals like soccer does.

examples.ko: 체육 시간에 핸드볼로 반 대항전을 했어요.
examples.en: In gym class we had a handball match between classes.

explain: 스포츠 종목 이름이에요. 축구에서 손으로 공을 건드리는 반칙도 '핸드볼'이라고 해서 '핸드볼 반칙'이라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is the name of a sport. In soccer, touching the ball with the hand is also called 핸드볼, so people sometimes say '핸드볼 반칙' (handball foul).

examples.en: On my trip to Japan I went to a karaoke place.
Karaoke is a machine for singing along to accompaniment.
I put a karaoke machine in the living room.
My friend likes karaoke, so we go often.
I liked the song I sang at karaoke.

examples.ko: 우리 동네에는 가라오케도 있고 노래방도 있어요.
examples.en: My neighborhood has both a karaoke bar and a noraebang.

explain: 한국에서 노래를 부르는 곳은 보통 '노래방'이라고 해요. '가라오케'는 일본에서 온 말이라 일본이나 외국의 시설을 이야기할 때 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: In Korea the usual word for a place to sing is '노래방'. '가라오케' came from Japan and is often used when talking about facilities in Japan or abroad.

examples.en: I bought a Korean workbook at the bookstore.
The explanations in this workbook are easy.
The workbook is thick, so I do a little every day.

examples.ko: 수학 문제집에 답이 틀린 곳이 있어요.
examples.en: There is a wrong answer in the math workbook.

examples.ko: 방학 때 문제집도 풀고 책도 읽었어요.
examples.en: During vacation I did workbooks and read books too.
My younger sibling prepares for the test with a workbook.

explain: '문제집을 풀다'처럼 '풀다'와 같이 써요. 교과서처럼 설명을 배우는 책이 아니라 연습 문제가 중심인 책이에요. 시험에 나왔던 문제를 모은 책은 '기출 문제집'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It goes with the verb '풀다': '문제집을 풀다' (work through a workbook). Unlike a textbook, it is mostly practice problems. A book of past exam questions is a '기출 문제집'.

examples.en: I serve coffee at a cafe.
I worked serving at a restaurant every weekend.
There are many customers, so it is hard to serve alone.
The server smiled kindly.

examples.ko: 제가 음식을 서빙할 테니 앉아 계세요.
examples.en: I will serve the food, so please stay seated.
After serving, I washed the dishes right away.

explain: 식당 아르바이트 이야기에서 '서빙을 하다', '서빙 알바'처럼 써요. 음식을 만드는 곳은 '주방', 손님 쪽에서 음식을 나르는 곳은 '홀'이라고 나눠 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It shows up in restaurant part-time talk: '서빙을 하다', '서빙 알바'. People sometimes split the work into '주방' (kitchen, where food is made) and '홀' (the floor, where food is carried to customers).

examples.en: I arrived at the test site an hour early.
The test site is a school gym.
Turn off your phone inside the test site.

examples.ko: 시험장이 너무 추워서 겉옷을 챙겨 갔어요.
examples.en: The test site was so cold that I brought a jacket.
I wandered around for a long time looking for the test site.

examples.ko: 시험장에서 만난 친구와 같이 점심을 먹었어요.
examples.en: I had lunch with a friend I met at the test site.

explain: 수능 같은 큰 시험에서는 미리 정해진 학교가 시험장이 돼요. 학교 안의 평소 시험은 보통 '교실'에서 봐요. '시험장에 들어가다', '시험장에서 나오다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: In big exams like the CSAT, a school decided in advance becomes the '시험장'. Ordinary tests at school are normally taken in the classroom. Say '시험장에 들어가다' (enter) or '시험장에서 나오다' (leave).

examples.en: He is a patriot who loves his country.
I read the story of a patriot in a book.
It is a class where we learn about patriots in history.
I remember the patriot who took part in the independence movement.
Being called a patriot is a great honor.

examples.ko: 그 애국자는 어려운 때에도 나라를 떠나지 않았어요.
examples.en: That patriot did not leave the country even in hard times.

explain: 나라를 위해 크게 힘쓴 사람에게 존경을 담아 써요. 일상에서 자기를 가리켜 '저는 애국자예요'라고 하면 조금 거창하게 들려요. '애국지사'는 특히 독립을 위해 싸운 분들께 써요.
explain_en: It is used with respect for someone who devoted themselves to the nation. Saying '저는 애국자예요' about yourself in daily life sounds a bit grand. '애국지사' is used especially for those who fought for independence.

examples.en: Skin color is different for each person.
I chose a foundation that matches my skin tone.

examples.ko: 피부색은 햇빛 때문에 변할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Skin color can change because of sunlight.

examples.ko: 피부색과 상관없이 모두 친구가 될 수 있어요.
examples.en: Everyone can be friends regardless of skin color.
The children expressed skin color in a drawing.

examples.ko: 피부색도 건강 상태를 알려 줄 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Skin color can sometimes tell you about your health.

explain: 사람의 피부 빛깔을 말할 때 써요. 사람의 피부색 이야기는 조심스러운 주제라서 차별하는 말이 되지 않게 신경 써야 해요. 예전 색연필의 '살색'은 지금 '살구색'이라는 이름으로 바뀌었어요.
explain_en: Use it for the color of a person's skin. Talking about people's skin color is a sensitive topic, so take care not to sound discriminatory. The old crayon name '살색' was changed to '살구색'.

examples.ko: 하이힐을 신고 오래 걸으면 발이 아파요.
examples.en: If you walk a long time in high heels, your feet hurt.
The new high heels are pretty but uncomfortable.

examples.ko: 면접 때 하이힐 대신 편한 구두를 신었어요.
examples.en: For the interview I wore comfortable shoes instead of high heels.
I wasn't used to high heels and almost fell.
Mom bought me both high heels and sneakers.
Climbing stairs in high heels is hard.

explain: 굽이 높은 구두를 가리켜요. 줄여서 '힐'이라고도 해요. 신는 동작은 '신다'를 써서 '하이힐을 신다'라고 말해요. 굽이 낮고 납작한 신발은 '플랫슈즈'라고 해요.
explain_en: It means shoes with high heels, and is shortened to '힐'. Use the verb '신다': '하이힐을 신다'. Low, flat shoes are called '플랫슈즈'.

examples.en: Could you give me the check, please?
I think the bill came out wrong.
A service charge is added to the bill.
I will take the bill.
Keep the bill too, just like a receipt.
The amount on the bill was less than I expected.

explain: 식당에서 '계산서 주세요'라고 해도 되고 '계산해 주세요'라고 해도 돼요. 영수증은 돈을 낸 뒤에 받는 종이, 계산서는 낼 돈이 적힌 종이로 나눠 생각하면 돼요.
explain_en: At a restaurant you can say either '계산서 주세요' or '계산해 주세요'. Think of a 영수증 (receipt) as the paper you get after paying, and a 계산서 as the paper listing what you owe.

examples.en: They scan the bar code at the checkout.
The bar code is torn, so it won't scan.

examples.ko: 바코드는 상품 정보를 기계로 읽게 해 줘요.
examples.en: A bar code lets a machine read product information.
Hold your phone camera up to the bar code.
You can also type in the bar code number.
A bar code also has to be clean to be read well.

explain: 마트 상품, 책, 택배 상자에서 볼 수 있어요. '바코드를 찍다', '바코드를 읽다'처럼 쓰고, 정사각형 모양의 'QR코드'와는 모양이 달라요.
explain_en: You can see it on supermarket goods, books, and delivery boxes. Say '바코드를 찍다' (scan) or '바코드를 읽다' (read). It looks different from a square 'QR코드'.

examples.en: I took one bite and said it was delicious.
I ate the whole cake in one mouthful.
Please cut the vegetables into bite-sized pieces.
The child begged for just one bite.

examples.ko: 한입씩 나눠 먹으면 모두 맛볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If we share it bite by bite, everyone can taste it.
I stuffed a mouthful of ramyeon in and smiled.

explain: '한입에 먹다'는 한 번에 다 먹는다는 쓰임이고, '한입 먹다'는 조금 베어 먹는다는 쓰임이에요. 조사에 따라 달라지니까 주의하세요. '한입만'은 조금만 달라고 할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: '한입에 먹다' means to eat all of it at once, while '한입 먹다' means to take a bite. The particle changes the meaning, so be careful. '한입만' is used when asking for just a little taste.

examples.en: Let's meet at the school's back gate.
The back gate closes at six in the evening.
The back gate is close, so I use it often.
If you go out the back entrance, you can see the subway station.
The front gate is good, but the back gate is convenient too.

examples.ko: 공사 중이라 후문을 찾는 손님들이 많았어요.
examples.en: Because of construction, many visitors were looking for the back entrance.

explain: 건물이나 학교의 뒤쪽 출입문을 가리켜요. 짝말은 '정문'이에요. 대학교나 학교 앞에서 '후문에서 만나요'처럼 약속 장소를 정할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It refers to the rear entrance of a building or school. Its counterpart is '정문' (main gate). It is also handy for meeting spots, as in '후문에서 만나요'.

en: counseling center; consultancy; counseling service agency

examples.en: If you have a worry, try going to a counseling center.

examples.ko: 이 상담소는 무료로 이야기를 들어 줘요.
examples.en: This counseling center listens to you for free.
The counseling center is on the third floor of the building.
My friend told me about a counseling center.
I talked with a counselor for an hour at the counseling center.
Some counseling centers also require a reservation.

explain: 고민이나 문제를 전문가와 이야기하러 가는 곳이에요. '법률 상담소', '청소년 상담소'처럼 앞에 분야를 붙여 써요. 학교 안에서는 '상담실'이라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a place where you go to talk about worries or problems with a professional. The field comes first, as in '법률 상담소' (legal) or '청소년 상담소' (youth). Inside a school it may be called '상담실'.

examples.en: The child colored in the picture.
When you finish coloring, show it to the teacher.
For coloring, use colored pencils, not a pencil.
It was quiet while they played the coloring game.
Painting the wall took a day.
Coloring takes as much time as drawing.

explain: '색칠을 하다'와 '색칠하다' 둘 다 써요. 그림이나 벽에 색을 입히는 일에 쓰고, 머리카락 색을 바꾸는 일은 '염색'이라고 해요.
explain_en: You can say either '색칠을 하다' or '색칠하다'. It is for putting color on a picture or a wall, while changing hair color is '염색'.

examples.en: My younger sibling is left-handed.

examples.ko: 왼손잡이는 가위를 쓰기 불편할 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Left-handed people sometimes find scissors awkward to use.
I bought a mouse for left-handed people.
I'm left-handed, so I write with my left hand.
There are families with many left-handed people.

examples.ko: 왼손잡이도 오른손을 잘 쓰는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some left-handed people also use their right hand well.

explain: 오른손잡이의 짝말이에요. 두 손을 다 잘 쓰는 사람은 '양손잡이'라고 해요. 도구를 살 때는 '왼손용'이라고 적힌 표시를 확인하면 돼요.
explain_en: It is the counterpart of '오른손잡이' (right-hander). Someone who uses both hands well is '양손잡이'. When buying tools, check for a label saying '왼손용' (for left hand).

examples.en: Our school holds a field day in autumn.
The field day was postponed because of rain.
I came first in the race at the field day.
On field day we bring gimbap.
The parents also took part in their child's field day.
I like May, when we have field day and go on picnics.

explain: 학교에서 달리기, 줄다리기 같은 경기를 하는 행사예요. 청군과 백군으로 팀을 나누기도 해요. 대학교나 회사의 큰 행사는 '체육대회'라고 하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is a school event with games like races and tug-of-war, sometimes split into blue and white teams. A large event at a university or company may be called '체육대회'.

examples.en: The doctor examines the patient.
The doctor examined the child's throat.

examples.ko: 오늘은 오후 두 시부터 진찰할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Today we can see patients from two in the afternoon.
After examining me, the doctor prescribed medicine.

examples.ko: 진찰하는 동안 환자는 조용히 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: The patient sat quietly during the examination.

examples.ko: 배가 아픈 이유를 알려면 직접 진찰해서 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: To know why your stomach hurts, the doctor has to examine you directly.

explain: 의사가 환자의 몸 상태를 살펴볼 때 쓰기 때문에 주어는 보통 의사예요. 환자가 병원에서 의사를 만나는 일은 '진료를 받다', '진찰을 받다'라고 해요. '제가 진찰했어요'는 의사가 아니면 어색해요.
explain_en: It is used when a doctor checks a patient, so the subject is normally the doctor. A patient seeing a doctor says '진료를 받다' or '진찰을 받다'. '제가 진찰했어요' sounds odd unless you are a doctor.

examples.en: Bedtime is eleven at night.
Don't look at your smartphone before bed.
In the dormitory, lights-out is at twelve.
I drink warm tea before going to bed.

examples.ko: 취침 후에는 방의 불을 꺼 주세요.
examples.en: After bedtime, please turn off the room light.
You get healthier if you go to bed regularly too.

explain: 잠자리에 드는 일을 격식 있게 나타내는 한자어예요. 일상 대화에서는 '자다', '잠자리에 들다'를 쓰고, 기숙사나 군대의 규칙, 안내문에서 '취침 시간'처럼 써요. 반대는 '기상'이에요.
explain_en: It is a formal Sino-Korean word for going to bed. In daily conversation use '자다' or '잠자리에 들다'; '취침 시간' (bedtime) appears in rules and notices at dormitories and the military. The opposite is '기상' (getting up).

examples.en: The child's eyes widened in surprise.
I was speechless with astonishment.
Surprise and joy rushed in all at once.
This result was a surprise to everyone.
The surprise soon turned into laughter.
The news gave a great surprise.

explain: '놀라다'를 명사로 만든 말이에요. '놀라움을 주다', '놀라움을 금치 못하다'처럼 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 써요. 말할 때는 '놀랐어요'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 결과를 보고 모두가 놀라움을 금치 못했어요.
phrases.nuance_ko: 너무 놀라서 놀란 마음을 감추기 어렵다는 격식 있는 표현이에요. 뉴스나 글에서 볼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal expression meaning one is so surprised that it is hard to hide the feeling. You see it in news and writing.
phrases.en_equiv: be unable to contain one's astonishment

explain_en: It is the noun form of '놀라다' (to be surprised). It often appears in writing and news, as in '놀라움을 주다' and '놀라움을 금치 못하다'. In speech, people say '놀랐어요'.

examples.en: In summer I go out wearing a straw hat.
My straw hat blew away in the wind.
A straw hat is nice because it blocks the sun.
I attached a ribbon to the straw hat.
I bought a straw hat at the beach.
I packed a straw hat and put on sunscreen too.

explain: 밀의 짚으로 엮어 만든 모자예요. 농부가 밭일할 때나 여름 바닷가에서 햇빛을 가리려고 많이 써요. 모자를 머리에 올리는 동작은 '쓰다'예요.
explain_en: It is a hat woven from wheat straw. Farmers wear it in the fields, and people wear it at the beach in summer to block the sun. The verb for putting on a hat is '쓰다'.

examples.en: I'm worried because my belly fat has increased lately.
I walk every day to lose belly fat.
Belly fat doesn't go away all at once.
My pants got tight because of my belly fat.
I cut back on snacks because I'm watching my belly fat.
I wonder if exercise reduces belly fat too.

explain: '배'와 '살'이 만나 사이시옷이 붙어 '뱃살'이 돼요. 배에 붙은 살이나 지방을 이야기할 때 써요. 다른 사람의 몸에 쓰면 평가처럼 들릴 수 있어서 조심하는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: '배' and '살' join with a linking ㅅ to become '뱃살'. Use it for fat on the stomach. Saying it about another person's body can sound like a judgment, so be careful.

examples.en: On Christmas I eat cake with my family.
As Christmas approaches, the streets sparkle.
Christmas is on December 25.
For Christmas we sang songs at church.
I haven't bought a Christmas gift yet.
This year Christmas is also a holiday, so I'm going on a trip.

explain: '크리스마스'와 같은 날이지만, 뉴스나 안내문 같은 글에서는 '성탄절'이라고도 써요. 친구와 이야기할 때는 '크리스마스'를 더 많이 말해요. 한국에서는 12월 25일이 공휴일이에요.
explain_en: It is the same day as '크리스마스', but news and notices also write '성탄절'. With friends, people tend to say '크리스마스'. December 25 is a public holiday in Korea.
